name: Allergic Rhinitis
summary: Sneezing, blocked nose, running and itching from an allergic response — seasonal or year-round, and often the root of recurring sinus trouble.
intro: Allergic rhinitis is inflammation of the nasal lining driven by an allergic response, most often to dust mite, pollen, mould or animal dander. It is frequently dismissed as 'just a cold that keeps coming back', but it disrupts sleep, concentration and work, and it underlies a great deal of recurrent sinusitis and poorly controlled asthma. Identifying triggers is as much a part of treatment as any prescription.
symptoms: Bouts of sneezing, often on waking
Clear, watery nasal discharge
Nasal blockage, frequently alternating sides
Itching of the nose, palate, eyes and ears
Post-nasal drip and throat clearing
Reduced sense of smell
Tiredness and poor concentration from disturbed sleep
causes: House dust mite — the leading year-round trigger in Kerala's humidity
Pollen, with a seasonal pattern
Mould spores, particularly in damp housing and the monsoon
Animal dander
Cockroach allergen
Strong smells, smoke and temperature change as non-allergic aggravators
Family history of allergy, asthma or eczema
treatment: History-led identification of triggers, with allergy testing where it will change management
Constitutional homeopathic prescription for the allergic tendency rather than the sneeze alone
Practical, specific allergen reduction at home — bedding, damp, ventilation
Assessment for associated asthma and sinusitis, which frequently travel with it
Guidance on saline irrigation and on the sensible use of antihistamines and nasal sprays

expectedResults.detail: Sneezing bouts and discharge usually respond before nasal blockage does.
Episodes tend to become shorter and less frequent; sleep improves.
The allergic tendency is constitutional. Exposure still provokes symptoms — the aim is a lower reaction to the same exposure.

faqs.question: Is this just a recurring cold?
faqs.answer: No. Colds are viral, last about a week and come with fever or body ache. Allergic rhinitis is itchy, sneezy, comes in bouts tied to exposure, and lasts as long as the exposure does.

faqs.question: Do I need allergy testing?
faqs.answer: Only when the result will change what you do. If your triggers are already obvious from the history, testing adds cost and little else — and positive results without matching symptoms are common and misleading.

name: Chronic Sinusitis
summary: Persistent sinus inflammation with blockage, facial pressure and discharge lasting beyond twelve weeks, often on a background of allergy.
intro: Chronic rhinosinusitis is inflammation of the sinuses and nasal lining persisting more than twelve weeks. It is rarely a simple infection that antibiotics keep failing to clear; more often there is an underlying allergic, structural or polypoid problem keeping the sinuses from draining. Treatment aims at that underlying picture. Where a scan shows polyps or a significant structural block, an ENT opinion is the right next step, and you will be told so.
symptoms: Nasal blockage or congestion lasting months
Thick nasal or post-nasal discharge
Facial pain, pressure or heaviness, worse on bending forward
Reduced or absent sense of smell
Headache, often frontal, and dental-type upper tooth pain
Persistent cough from post-nasal drip
Fatigue and poor sleep
causes: Underlying allergic rhinitis
Nasal polyps
Deviated nasal septum and other structural narrowing
Repeated or inadequately treated acute infections
Dental infection of the upper molars
Humidity, dust and occupational irritants
Overuse of decongestant nasal drops, which causes rebound blockage
treatment: Assessment of the underlying driver — allergy, polyps or structure — rather than treating each episode as fresh infection
Homeopathic prescription for the chronic inflammatory and catarrhal tendency
Saline nasal irrigation technique, which is genuinely useful and usually done wrongly
Withdrawal from long-term decongestant drops where these are in use
ENT referral for CT imaging or surgical assessment where polyps or obstruction are likely

expectedResults.detail: Discharge, facial pressure and headache frequency usually ease first.
Blockage and smell improve more slowly; acute flares become less frequent.
Where polyps or a structural block are the cause, medicine alone has limits. Surgery is not a failure of treatment — sometimes it is the correct treatment.

faqs.question: Why do antibiotics keep not working?
faqs.answer: Because chronic sinusitis is usually inflammation with poor drainage, not persistent bacterial infection. Repeated antibiotic courses treat something that is not the main problem — and leave resistance behind.

faqs.question: Do I need sinus surgery?
faqs.answer: Most people do not. It becomes the right option when polyps or structural obstruction are preventing drainage and medical treatment has been given a fair trial. A CT scan and an ENT opinion answer that question properly.

name: Acid Reflux & GERD
summary: Burning behind the breastbone, regurgitation and throat symptoms when stomach contents flow back into the oesophagus.
intro: Reflux happens when the valve between the stomach and oesophagus does not close reliably, letting acid back up. Occasional reflux is normal; when it is frequent enough to cause symptoms or damage, it is called GERD. It responds well to specific changes in eating, timing and posture — often better than to another course of tablets. Alarm symptoms such as difficulty swallowing or weight loss need endoscopy, not more medicine.
symptoms: Burning behind the breastbone, worse after meals and on lying down
Sour or bitter regurgitation into the throat
Persistent throat clearing, hoarseness or a lump sensation
Chronic dry cough, particularly at night
Bloating and early fullness
Disturbed sleep from night-time symptoms
Dental erosion in longstanding cases
causes: Weak or relaxing lower oesophageal sphincter
Hiatus hernia
Overweight, particularly abdominal
Large meals, late dinners and lying down soon after eating
Spicy, fried and fatty foods; coffee, tea and alcohol
Smoking
NSAIDs and certain other medications
Stress and irregular meal timing
treatment: Careful history to separate reflux from cardiac and gallbladder pain — chest pain is never assumed to be acid
Homeopathic prescription for the digestive pattern, appetite and stress component
Concrete guidance on meal timing, portion size and the last-meal-to-bed interval
Positional and weight measures, which outperform most dietary folklore
Referral for endoscopy where there is difficulty swallowing, weight loss, vomiting blood, anaemia or onset after 45

expectedResults.detail: Meal timing and portion changes often produce the fastest relief of night symptoms.
Frequency and intensity of burning typically reduce; throat symptoms take longer.
Reflux relapses readily when eating patterns slip. Long-term acid-suppressing medication should only be reduced with your physician's involvement.

faqs.question: Is chest burning always acidity?
faqs.answer: No — and this is important. Cardiac pain is regularly mistaken for acidity, particularly in people with diabetes, high blood pressure or a family history. Chest pain with sweating, breathlessness or arm and jaw pain is an emergency, not a stomach problem.

faqs.question: Can I stop my pantoprazole?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but not abruptly — stopping suddenly causes a rebound surge of acid that feels like the condition returning worse. Any reduction is planned gradually and with your prescribing physician.

name: Irritable Bowel Syndrome
summary: Recurrent abdominal pain with altered bowel habit and no structural disease — real, common, and closely tied to stress and diet.
intro: IBS is a disorder of gut-brain interaction: the bowel is structurally normal but functions and signals abnormally. The pain is real, and being told 'the tests are normal' helps no one. Diagnosis rests on a characteristic symptom pattern once alarm features have been excluded. Treatment works on the whole picture — diet, stress, sleep and bowel habit — because in IBS these are not peripheral factors, they are the mechanism.
symptoms: Recurrent abdominal pain, often relieved by passing stool
Alternating constipation and loose stools, or a predominance of one
Bloating and visible abdominal distension, worse through the day
Urgency, or a feeling of incomplete evacuation
Mucus in the stool
Symptoms clearly worsened by stress
Fatigue and disturbed sleep
causes: Altered gut-brain signalling and visceral hypersensitivity
Disturbed gut motility
Onset after an episode of gastroenteritis in some patients
Changes in gut microbial balance
Anxiety, depression and chronic stress
Specific dietary triggers, including fermentable carbohydrates
Irregular meals and poor sleep
treatment: Exclusion of alarm features and of coeliac disease, thyroid disease and inflammatory bowel disease where indicated
Constitutional homeopathic prescription — IBS is a classic condition where the individual pattern, not the label, guides the remedy
Structured dietary work, including a properly supervised low-FODMAP trial where appropriate
Direct attention to stress, anxiety and sleep as part of treatment, not as an afterthought
Gastroenterology referral for bleeding, weight loss, anaemia, nocturnal symptoms or onset after 50

expectedResults.detail: Bloating and pain frequency are usually the earliest measures to shift.
Bowel habit becomes more predictable; confidence about leaving the house improves, which patients often value most.
IBS runs a relapsing course, particularly under stress. The realistic goal is control and confidence, not permanent absence of symptoms.

faqs.question: My tests are all normal — is this in my head?
faqs.answer: No. IBS is a genuine disorder of how the gut functions and how pain signals are processed. Normal tests are what confirm the diagnosis, not what dismiss it.

faqs.question: Should I stop eating wheat and dairy?
faqs.answer: Only if there is a clear, reproducible link for you. Blanket elimination narrows the diet, rarely helps, and can mask coeliac disease if wheat is dropped before testing. Structured trials beat guesswork.

name: Chronic Constipation
summary: Infrequent, hard or difficult stools over months — addressed at the cause rather than through escalating laxative use.
intro: Constipation is defined by difficulty and consistency rather than by a fixed daily schedule. It becomes chronic when it persists for months, and it commonly brings straining, piles, fissures and a quiet dependence on laxatives. Diet, fluid, activity, medication side effects and thyroid function all contribute. Treatment addresses those, and stimulant laxative use is reduced deliberately rather than continued indefinitely.
symptoms: Fewer than three bowel movements a week, or a clear change from your normal
Hard, dry, lumpy stools
Straining and a sense of incomplete evacuation
Abdominal bloating and discomfort
Need to use fingers or change position to pass stool
Anal pain, fissure or bleeding from hard stool
Reliance on laxatives to open the bowels at all
causes: Low dietary fibre and inadequate fluid
Physical inactivity
Habitually ignoring the urge to pass stool
Hypothyroidism, diabetes and neurological conditions
Medications: iron, calcium, opioids, some antidepressants and antacids
Pregnancy and the post-partum period
Long-term stimulant laxative use, which worsens the underlying problem
Pelvic floor dysfunction
treatment: Exclusion of thyroid disease, and of red flags such as bleeding, weight loss or recent onset in later life
Review of every medication being taken — this frequently identifies the cause
Homeopathic prescription for the individual bowel pattern and general constitution
Specific dietary, fluid and toilet-habit guidance, including posture and timing
A planned reduction of stimulant laxatives rather than abrupt withdrawal

expectedResults.detail: Stool consistency and ease of passing usually change before frequency does.
A more regular pattern establishes, with reducing need for laxatives.
Relapse follows when fibre, fluid and activity slip. Where pelvic floor dysfunction is the cause, specialist physiotherapy is more effective than any medicine.

faqs.question: Is it necessary to pass stool every day?
faqs.answer: No. Anywhere from three times a day to three times a week can be normal, provided stools are soft and pass without straining. Difficulty matters more than frequency.

faqs.question: Are daily laxatives harmful?
faqs.answer: Long-term stimulant laxatives can leave the bowel less responsive over time and mask an underlying cause. That is precisely why the plan includes reducing them, rather than simply adding something on top.

name: Piles (Haemorrhoids)
summary: Swollen anal cushions causing bleeding, itching, prolapse and pain — manageable medically, though advanced grades need surgery.
intro: Haemorrhoids are engorged vascular cushions in the anal canal, and they are extremely common. Straining from constipation is the usual driver, which is why treating the bowel matters more than treating the piles. Grade determines what is realistic: early grades usually settle with medical management, while prolapsed piles that do not reduce need surgical treatment. Critically, rectal bleeding is never assumed to be piles without examination.
symptoms: Bright red bleeding at the end of passing stool, often on the paper or in the pan
A lump felt at the anus, which may reduce spontaneously or need pushing back
Itching and irritation around the anus
Mucus discharge and a feeling of incomplete evacuation
Severe pain if a pile thromboses
Discomfort on prolonged sitting
causes: Chronic constipation and straining
Prolonged sitting, including long hours on the toilet with a phone
Pregnancy and childbirth
Heavy lifting
Low-fibre diet and inadequate fluid
Overweight
Chronic cough and, less commonly, liver disease
treatment: Examination to confirm the diagnosis and grade — bleeding is never attributed to piles by history alone
Homeopathic prescription for the bleeding, pain and venous tendency
Treating the constipation, which is the actual driver in most cases
Practical measures: fibre, fluid, sitz baths, toilet posture, and time limits on sitting
Surgical referral for grade III–IV piles, persistent bleeding or thrombosis, and for anyone over 40 with new rectal bleeding

expectedResults.detail: Bleeding and pain usually respond first, particularly once stools soften.
Prolapse and discomfort improve in earlier grades as the bowel pattern normalises.
Grade III and IV piles are structural and generally need a procedure. Recurrence follows if constipation returns, whatever treatment was used.

faqs.question: Bleeding from the back passage — is it definitely piles?
faqs.answer: Not until it has been examined. Piles are the commonest cause, but colorectal cancer can bleed in exactly the same way, and assuming piles is one of the ways serious disease gets missed. New bleeding over the age of 40, or with weight loss or a change in bowel habit, needs proper assessment.

faqs.question: Can I avoid surgery?
faqs.answer: Often, in early grades, if the constipation is genuinely dealt with. Piles that prolapse and will not go back are a structural problem, and you will be told honestly when that point has been reached.

name: Rheumatoid Arthritis
summary: Autoimmune inflammation of the joint lining — treated alongside rheumatology care, because delay in DMARD therapy costs joints permanently.
intro: Rheumatoid arthritis is a systemic autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the joint lining, typically affecting the small joints of hands and feet symmetrically. Joint damage happens early, and modern rheumatology treats it aggressively for exactly that reason. Homeopathic treatment here supports pain, stiffness, fatigue and general wellbeing alongside that care. It is not an alternative to DMARDs, and delaying them causes irreversible harm.
symptoms: Symmetrical pain and swelling of the small joints of hands and feet
Morning stiffness lasting more than an hour
Warm, tender, swollen joints
Marked fatigue and general unwellness
Low-grade fever and weight loss during active disease
Firm nodules near the elbows
Reduced grip strength and difficulty with fine tasks
causes: Autoimmune attack on the synovial joint lining
Genetic susceptibility with a family history in many patients
Smoking, the strongest known environmental risk factor
Hormonal factors — women are affected far more often
Infections and gut microbial factors as proposed triggers
Physical or emotional stress as a reported precipitant
treatment: Review of RA factor, anti-CCP, inflammatory markers and current rheumatology treatment
Homeopathic prescription for pain, stiffness, fatigue and the individual's overall pattern
Emphasis on continuing DMARD therapy — this is stated clearly and repeatedly
Attention to sleep, mood and gentle joint-preserving activity
Immediate referral if joints are swelling and treatment is not in place, since early months determine long-term damage

expectedResults.detail: Pain, morning stiffness duration and fatigue are the practical measures used.
Many patients report better function and fewer flare days alongside their rheumatology treatment.
Existing joint damage and deformity do not reverse. Disease-modifying decisions belong to your rheumatologist, based on inflammatory markers and examination.

faqs.question: Can I stop methotrexate and take only homeopathy?
faqs.answer: No. DMARDs prevent joint destruction, and the damage caused by stopping them is permanent. This clinic treats alongside rheumatology care, and will say so plainly rather than take on a patient by implying otherwise.

faqs.question: Is rheumatoid arthritis the same as ordinary joint pain with age?
faqs.answer: No. Osteoarthritis is wear-related, worse with use and stiff for minutes in the morning. Rheumatoid arthritis is autoimmune, symmetrical, stiff for over an hour, and it damages joints — which is why it is treated urgently.

name: Osteoarthritis
summary: Wear-related joint pain, most often of the knees, where weight and muscle strength influence the outcome more than any medicine.
intro: Osteoarthritis is the gradual loss of joint cartilage with associated bone and soft tissue change, most commonly affecting knees, hips, hands and the spine. In India knee osteoarthritis is very common, and floor-sitting, squatting and excess weight all contribute. The evidence is unambiguous on two points: weight reduction and quadriceps strengthening change symptoms more than any tablet. Treatment here builds around that rather than around it.
symptoms: Joint pain worse with use and relieved by rest
Stiffness after sitting still, easing within about 30 minutes of moving
Grating or crackling sensation on movement
Reduced range of movement, particularly deep knee bending
Swelling around the joint after activity
Difficulty with stairs, squatting and floor sitting
Visible bony enlargement of finger joints
causes: Age-related cartilage wear
Excess body weight, which multiplies load through the knee
Previous joint injury or surgery
Occupational squatting, kneeling and heavy lifting
Weak quadriceps and poor joint stability
Genetic predisposition, particularly in hand osteoarthritis
Malalignment such as bow legs
treatment: Examination and review of X-rays to establish grade and to exclude inflammatory arthritis
Homeopathic prescription for pain, stiffness and the individual's response pattern
A structured quadriceps and hip strengthening programme — the single most effective intervention available
Weight reduction guidance where relevant, with realistic targets
Orthopaedic referral where the joint is severely damaged and replacement should be discussed

expectedResults.detail: Pain intensity and stiffness often ease first, especially once strengthening exercises are being done consistently.
Walking distance, stair climbing and daily function typically improve alongside muscle strength.
Cartilage already lost does not regrow — with any treatment. The aim is comfortable function; where the joint is bone-on-bone, replacement surgery is the honest recommendation.

faqs.question: Can lost cartilage be regrown?
faqs.answer: No. No medicine, supplement or injection currently available regrows worn cartilage, whatever the advertising says. What can genuinely improve is pain, muscle support and function.

faqs.question: Should I avoid walking to protect my knees?
faqs.answer: No — inactivity weakens the muscles that protect the joint and usually makes pain worse. What is worth avoiding is deep squatting, kneeling and stairs where they hurt. Appropriate movement is treatment, not risk.

name: Gout
summary: Sudden, severe attacks of joint pain from uric acid crystals — usually the big toe, and increasingly common with modern diets.
intro: Gout is caused by monosodium urate crystals forming in a joint when blood uric acid is persistently high. The classic attack comes on overnight in the big toe with pain so severe that a bedsheet is intolerable. Between attacks there may be nothing at all, which is why many people stop treatment and end up with joint damage and tophi. Attack relief and long-term urate control are two separate goals, and both are addressed.
symptoms: Sudden severe pain, usually starting at night, most often in the big toe
Redness, heat and marked swelling of the joint
Pain so intense that light touch is unbearable
Attacks lasting days to a couple of weeks, then resolving completely
Involvement of ankle, knee, wrist or fingers in later attacks
Chalky white lumps (tophi) around joints or ears in longstanding disease
Kidney stones in some patients
causes: Persistently raised blood uric acid
Diets high in red meat, organ meat and shellfish
Alcohol, particularly beer
Sugary drinks and fructose
Diuretics and certain other medications
Obesity, metabolic syndrome and kidney impairment
Dehydration, and sometimes a sudden change in diet or fasting
treatment: Confirmation of gout rather than septic arthritis or pseudogout — a hot swollen joint with fever is an emergency
Homeopathic prescription for the acute attack and for the constitutional tendency between attacks
Concrete dietary and alcohol guidance, alongside attention to hydration
Review of medications, particularly diuretics, that raise urate
Coordination with your physician on urate-lowering therapy where attacks are frequent or tophi have formed

expectedResults.detail: Acute attack pain and swelling settle over roughly this period with treatment.
With dietary change and treatment, attack frequency usually falls. Serum uric acid is rechecked to assess objectively.

Tophi and joint damage already present do not reverse quickly. Where urate-lowering therapy is prescribed, it works only if continued between attacks — the commonest reason gout persists is stopping it when the pain goes.

faqs.question: My uric acid is high but I have no pain — do I need treatment?
faqs.answer: Asymptomatic hyperuricaemia is usually managed through diet, weight and hydration rather than medication. It is worth attention, because it often travels with metabolic problems that matter more than the number itself.

faqs.question: Can I ever eat non-vegetarian food again?
faqs.answer: Usually in moderation, once attacks are controlled. Organ meats, shellfish and beer are the main offenders. Complete lifelong restriction is rarely necessary and rarely sustained.

name: Cervical Spondylosis
summary: Age- and posture-related neck degeneration causing pain, stiffness, headache and — when nerves are compressed — arm symptoms.
intro: Cervical spondylosis is degenerative change in the neck's discs and joints. It is nearly universal on scans after middle age, and most of it causes no symptoms at all — which is why treatment follows examination, not the radiology report. Where symptoms do occur, posture and desk and phone habits are usually central. Weakness, numbness or clumsiness in the hands, or any disturbance of balance or bladder, needs urgent assessment.
symptoms: Neck pain and stiffness, worse after prolonged desk or phone use
Grating sensation on turning the head
Headache starting at the back of the head
Pain radiating to the shoulder blade or down an arm
Tingling or numbness in the fingers
Weakness of grip in nerve compression
Dizziness on certain neck movements
causes: Age-related disc dehydration and facet joint degeneration
Prolonged forward-head posture at desks and screens
Sustained phone use with the neck flexed
Previous neck injury, including whiplash
Heavy load carrying on the head or shoulders
Weak deep neck and scapular musculature
Poor sleeping position and unsuitable pillows
treatment: Neurological examination — the priority is identifying nerve or cord compression, not describing the X-ray
Homeopathic prescription for pain, stiffness and the individual's pain pattern
A specific posture, workstation and phone-use correction
A graded deep neck flexor and scapular strengthening programme
Urgent referral for progressive weakness, hand clumsiness, gait disturbance or bladder symptoms

expectedResults.detail: Pain and stiffness usually respond first, often noticeably once workstation changes are made.
Headache frequency and arm symptoms improve as posture and strength change.
Degenerative change on the scan does not reverse and does not need to. Recurrence follows a return to old postures more reliably than anything else.

faqs.question: My scan looks bad — does that mean my neck is badly damaged?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Degenerative changes appear on the scans of most people over 40, including those with no pain at all. What matters clinically is the examination, not the report wording.

faqs.question: When is neck pain an emergency?
faqs.answer: Progressive weakness in the arms or legs, clumsy hands, unsteady walking, or any bladder or bowel disturbance. Those suggest cord compression and need immediate assessment, not a course of treatment.

name: Insomnia & Sleep Disorders
summary: Persistent difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep or waking refreshed — treated at its causes rather than with indefinite sedatives.
intro: Chronic insomnia means poor sleep at least three nights a week for three months or more, with daytime consequences. It is rarely a stand-alone problem: anxiety, depression, pain, reflux, thyroid disease, sleep apnoea, caffeine and screen habits all appear regularly. Sedatives are easy to start and hard to stop, and tolerance builds. Treatment here identifies the driver, applies the behavioural work that has the best evidence, and prescribes constitutionally.
symptoms: Lying awake for long periods trying to fall asleep
Repeated waking through the night, with difficulty returning to sleep
Waking too early and unable to sleep again
Waking unrefreshed however long the night lasted
Daytime fatigue, irritability and poor concentration
Anxiety about sleep itself as bedtime approaches
Reliance on sedatives or alcohol to fall asleep
causes: Anxiety, depression and chronic stress
Irregular sleep timing, shift work and late screen use
Caffeine, nicotine and alcohol — the last fragments sleep even as it induces it
Pain, reflux, nocturia and breathlessness
Obstructive sleep apnoea, frequently missed
Thyroid dysfunction, menopause and certain medications
Conditioned arousal — the bed itself becoming a cue for wakefulness
treatment: Identifying the underlying driver, with specific screening for sleep apnoea and mood disorder
Constitutional homeopathic prescription based on the sleep pattern, dreams, timing and temperament
Structured behavioural sleep work, which has the strongest evidence base of any insomnia treatment
A planned reduction of sedatives where these are in long-term use, never abruptly
Referral for sleep study where snoring, witnessed apnoea or excessive daytime sleepiness is present

expectedResults.detail: Sleep onset time and night-time anxiety are usually the first to change.
Sleep continuity and daytime energy improve as the pattern re-establishes.
Relapse under stress is normal and does not undo progress. Where sleep apnoea is the cause, CPAP treats it and medicine does not.

faqs.question: Can I stop my sleeping tablets?
faqs.answer: Usually, but gradually and with your prescriber involved. Abrupt withdrawal of benzodiazepines or Z-drugs causes rebound insomnia far worse than the original problem, and in some cases is medically unsafe.

faqs.question: How many hours should I be sleeping?
faqs.answer: Most adults need seven to nine, but the range is genuinely wide. Waking refreshed and functioning well through the day matters more than hitting a number — and anxiously counting hours makes insomnia worse.

name: Anxiety & Stress Disorders
summary: Persistent worry, tension and physical symptoms of arousal — treated with the seriousness it deserves, and alongside psychiatric care where needed.
intro: Anxiety becomes a disorder when it is disproportionate, persistent and interferes with living. It shows itself physically as much as mentally: palpitations, chest tightness, gut symptoms, tremor, headache and hair fall are all routine presentations. Homeopathic treatment can help meaningfully. It is not a substitute for psychiatric care in severe illness, and anyone with thoughts of self-harm should be seen urgently by a psychiatrist — that is said clearly, not implied.
symptoms: Persistent worry that is hard to control
Restlessness, irritability and being permanently on edge
Palpitations, chest tightness and breathlessness
Tremor, sweating and dry mouth
Gut symptoms — nausea, loose stools, a knot in the stomach
Difficulty falling asleep from a racing mind
Panic attacks with an overwhelming sense of impending disaster
Hair fall and skin flares tracking with stressful periods
causes: Genetic and temperamental predisposition
Chronic life stress: work, finances, caregiving, relationships
Trauma and adverse experiences
Thyroid dysfunction, which mimics anxiety closely
Caffeine, nicotine, alcohol and certain medications
Chronic sleep deprivation
Physical illness and chronic pain
treatment: Assessment of severity, and specific screening for depression and self-harm risk
Thyroid testing, since hyperthyroidism presents as anxiety often enough to warrant checking
Constitutional homeopathic prescription based on the character of the anxiety, its triggers and physical expression
Practical work on sleep, caffeine, activity and breathing techniques
Referral for psychological therapy or psychiatric care where severity warrants it — and continuation of any existing psychiatric medication

expectedResults.detail: Sleep and the physical symptoms — palpitations, gut, tremor — often ease before the worry itself.
Baseline tension typically falls; panic episodes become less frequent and less overwhelming.
Anxiety fluctuates with life circumstances. Psychiatric medication should never be stopped abruptly or without the prescriber's involvement.

faqs.question: Can I stop my psychiatric medication?
faqs.answer: Not on our advice and not abruptly. Antidepressants and anxiolytics require planned tapering under the prescriber's supervision; sudden withdrawal can be genuinely harmful. Treatment here runs alongside that care.

faqs.question: Could my palpitations be a heart problem?
faqs.answer: They can be, and are not assumed to be anxiety. Anyone with palpitations, chest pain or breathlessness gets appropriate cardiac assessment first — attributing physical symptoms to anxiety without checking is how serious illness gets missed.

name: Chronic Fatigue
summary: Persistent exhaustion not explained by exertion and not relieved by rest — investigated properly before it is treated.
intro: Persistent fatigue is one of the most common reasons people seek treatment, and one of the most frequently dismissed. It has a long list of treatable causes — anaemia, thyroid disease, diabetes, vitamin D and B12 deficiency, sleep apnoea, depression — and the first job is to find or exclude them. Only then does constitutional treatment make sense. Fatigue lasting more than a few weeks deserves investigation, not reassurance.
symptoms: Exhaustion out of proportion to activity, not relieved by sleep
Feeling worse for a day or more after modest exertion
Unrefreshing sleep
Poor concentration and memory — the 'brain fog' patients describe
Muscle and joint aching without swelling
Headache, dizziness and light-headedness on standing
Low mood and loss of interest
Hair fall accompanying prolonged fatigue
causes: Iron deficiency anaemia — extremely common, particularly in women
Hypothyroidism
Vitamin D and B12 deficiency
Diabetes and other metabolic disease
Obstructive sleep apnoea and chronic sleep deprivation
Depression and chronic anxiety
Post-viral fatigue following infection
Chronic infection, kidney or liver disease
treatment: A proper workup first: haemoglobin and iron studies, thyroid function, blood sugar, vitamin D and B12, and more where indicated
Treating what the investigations find — much fatigue has a specific and correctable cause
Constitutional homeopathic prescription where no single cause explains the picture
Structured attention to sleep, activity pacing and nutrition
Referral for sleep study, psychiatric or specialist assessment where indicated

expectedResults.detail: Where a deficiency or thyroid problem is found and corrected, improvement can be substantial and relatively quick.
Where no single cause is identified, recovery is gradual and paced. Sleep and cognitive symptoms often improve before physical stamina.
Post-viral and unexplained fatigue can be prolonged and relapsing. Pushing through it reliably makes it worse, so pacing is part of treatment rather than a concession.

faqs.question: All my reports are normal — what now?
faqs.answer: Normal results are useful: they exclude the causes that need specific treatment. Persistent fatigue with normal investigations is real and is treated constitutionally, with attention to sleep, pacing and mood.

faqs.question: Will vitamin injections fix it?
faqs.answer: Only if you are actually deficient. Injecting vitamins into someone with normal levels is a common practice with no benefit beyond the cost of it. Treatment here follows the results, not the request.

name: Irregular Periods
summary: Cycles that are unpredictable, too far apart or too frequent — a symptom with many causes, investigated before it is treated.
intro: A cycle between 21 and 35 days is normal, and some variation is expected. Irregularity becomes worth investigating when it is persistent, a clear change from your own pattern, or accompanied by other symptoms. PCOS, thyroid disease, raised prolactin, weight change and stress are the usual culprits, and they are distinguished by examination and blood tests rather than assumption. Any bleeding after menopause, or between periods, is assessed separately and promptly.
symptoms: Cycles shorter than 21 days or longer than 35
Periods skipped for months at a time
Unpredictable timing with no discernible pattern
Marked variation in flow from one cycle to the next
Spotting between periods
Acne, excess facial hair or weight gain alongside the irregularity
Difficulty conceiving
causes: Polycystic ovary syndrome
Thyroid dysfunction, both under- and overactive
Raised prolactin
Significant weight gain or loss, and low body fat from intensive exercise
Chronic stress and disturbed sleep
Perimenopause
Uterine causes such as fibroids or polyps
Hormonal contraception and certain medications
treatment: A proper workup: thyroid function, prolactin, androgens and pelvic ultrasound where indicated
Constitutional homeopathic prescription based on the cycle pattern and the whole clinical picture
Treatment directed at the identified cause rather than at the symptom of irregularity
Attention to weight, sleep, stress and nutrition, which influence cycles considerably
Gynaecology referral for structural findings or for bleeding between periods and after menopause

expectedResults.detail: Associated symptoms — energy, mood, acne, pain — often respond before the cycle itself.
Cycles typically need two to three months to reflect any change, since each is set up well in advance.
Where PCOS or thyroid disease is the cause, this is long-term management rather than a fixed course of treatment.

faqs.question: How long before my periods become regular?
faqs.answer: Realistically, three to six months at minimum — a cycle is set in motion months before it appears, so nothing changes quickly. Anyone promising regular cycles within weeks is not describing how the ovary works.

faqs.question: Do I need a scan?
faqs.answer: Often yes, particularly with prolonged irregularity, heavy bleeding or difficulty conceiving. A pelvic ultrasound and a short blood panel answer most of the questions that guesswork cannot.

name: Painful Periods (Dysmenorrhoea)
summary: Menstrual cramping severe enough to disrupt daily life — never dismissed as something to be endured, and always checked for a cause.
intro: Period pain is common; pain that keeps you out of school or work, needs increasing painkillers or is getting worse over time is not something to accept. Primary dysmenorrhoea comes from prostaglandin-driven uterine contraction. Secondary dysmenorrhoea has an underlying cause — endometriosis, adenomyosis, fibroids or infection — and it is missed far too often. Which one you have is the first thing to establish.
symptoms: Cramping lower abdominal pain starting just before or with bleeding
Pain radiating to the lower back and inner thighs
Nausea, vomiting or loose stools with the pain
Headache, fatigue and dizziness during the period
Pain requiring painkillers to get through the day
Pain that has worsened over the years — a signal of a secondary cause
Pain during intercourse or when passing stool during periods
causes: Prostaglandin release causing strong uterine contraction
Endometriosis
Adenomyosis
Uterine fibroids
Pelvic inflammatory disease
Intrauterine devices in some women
Structural anomalies of the uterus or cervix
treatment: History and examination aimed specifically at separating primary from secondary dysmenorrhoea
Pelvic ultrasound where the pattern suggests a structural or endometriotic cause
Constitutional homeopathic prescription based on the character, timing and modalities of the pain
Practical measures: heat, activity, magnesium and sleep, which help more than they are given credit for
Gynaecology referral where endometriosis or adenomyosis is suspected — this needs specialist assessment

expectedResults.detail: Intensity and duration of pain are the measures used; some women notice change in the first cycle, many do not.
Reduced need for painkillers and fewer days lost is the practical goal.
Where endometriosis or adenomyosis is present, this is long-term management alongside gynaecological care, not a short course.

faqs.question: Is severe period pain normal?
faqs.answer: Some cramping is. Pain that stops you working or studying, needs escalating painkillers, or is worsening year on year is not normal and deserves investigation rather than endurance.

faqs.question: Will it improve after marriage or childbirth?
faqs.answer: This advice is given constantly and is not reliable. Primary dysmenorrhoea does often ease after childbirth; endometriosis and adenomyosis do not, and waiting on that hope delays diagnosis by years.

name: Heavy Menstrual Bleeding
summary: Periods heavy enough to cause flooding, clots or anaemia — a common cause of iron deficiency and, with it, hair fall.
intro: Heavy menstrual bleeding is defined by its effect on you, not by a measured volume: soaking through protection hourly, passing large clots, flooding at night, or being anaemic because of it. It is a frequent and under-recognised cause of iron deficiency in Indian women, and iron deficiency is one of the commonest reversible causes of hair fall — which is why the two are treated together here.
symptoms: Soaking through a pad or tampon every hour or two
Passing clots larger than a rupee coin
Bleeding lasting more than seven days
Flooding at night or needing double protection
Fatigue, breathlessness and palpitations from anaemia
Pallor, brittle nails and diffuse hair fall
Restricting work or travel around period days
causes: Uterine fibroids
Adenomyosis
Endometrial polyps
Hormonal imbalance, particularly around perimenopause and after menarche
Thyroid dysfunction
Bleeding and clotting disorders
Intrauterine devices and anticoagulant medication
Endometrial pathology, which must be excluded in older women
treatment: Haemoglobin and iron studies at the outset — anaemia here is the rule rather than the exception
Thyroid testing and pelvic ultrasound to identify structural causes
Constitutional homeopathic prescription for the bleeding pattern and general constitution
Correction of iron deficiency, which also addresses the associated hair fall
Gynaecology referral for fibroids, polyps, or any post-menopausal or irregular intermenstrual bleeding

expectedResults.detail: Flow volume and duration are tracked cycle by cycle rather than judged on impression.
As bleeding and iron stores improve, fatigue and hair fall usually follow — hair lagging some months behind the blood results.
Where fibroids or adenomyosis are the cause, medicine manages the bleeding; it does not remove the fibroid. Surgical options are discussed honestly when they are the better answer.

faqs.question: How do I know if my periods are actually heavy?
faqs.answer: Practical markers: soaking protection hourly, clots bigger than a rupee coin, bleeding beyond seven days, flooding at night, or a low haemoglobin. If any apply, it is worth assessing rather than comparing with friends.

faqs.question: Could this be why my hair is falling?
faqs.answer: Very likely, in part. Heavy periods deplete iron, and low ferritin is one of the most common and most correctable contributors to diffuse hair fall in women. Both are checked at the same consultation here.

name: Premenstrual Syndrome
summary: Physical and emotional symptoms in the luteal phase that resolve with bleeding — real, cyclical, and not something to apologise for.
intro: PMS is a cluster of symptoms appearing in the one to two weeks before a period and settling once bleeding starts. The defining feature is the timing, which is why a symptom diary over two or three cycles is worth more than any single consultation impression. A smaller number of women have premenstrual dysphoric disorder, where mood symptoms are severe enough to damage relationships and work; that needs recognising rather than minimising.
symptoms: Irritability, mood swings and tearfulness before periods
Anxiety or low mood lifting within a day or two of bleeding starting
Breast tenderness and fullness
Bloating, weight gain and fluid retention
Headache or migraine timed to the cycle
Food cravings, particularly sweet or salty
Fatigue, poor concentration and disturbed sleep
Acne and skin flares in the same window
causes: Sensitivity to normal cyclical hormone fluctuation rather than abnormal hormone levels
Serotonin changes in the luteal phase
Underlying anxiety or depression, which amplifies premenstrual symptoms
Thyroid dysfunction
High caffeine, alcohol and salt intake
Poor sleep and chronic stress
Nutritional factors, including low calcium and magnesium
treatment: A symptom diary across two or three cycles to establish the timing pattern objectively
Screening for thyroid disease and for underlying mood disorder
Constitutional homeopathic prescription reflecting the emotional and physical picture together
Specific dietary, exercise and sleep measures for the luteal phase
Psychiatric referral where premenstrual dysphoric disorder is severe — this is a recognised disorder, not a character trait

expectedResults.detail: The diary itself often clarifies the pattern and reduces the sense of unpredictability.
Symptom intensity typically eases; the premenstrual window becomes less disruptive.
PMS continues as long as cycles do, and worsens for some in perimenopause. It is managed rather than removed.

faqs.question: Are my hormone levels abnormal?
faqs.answer: Usually not. PMS reflects sensitivity to normal hormonal fluctuation rather than abnormal levels, which is why routine hormone testing in typical PMS rarely adds anything.

faqs.question: Is it normal to feel this low before periods?
faqs.answer: Mild mood change is common. Feeling hopeless, uncontrollably angry or unable to function is not, and it has a name — premenstrual dysphoric disorder. It is treatable, and it should not be dismissed as being oversensitive.

name: Menopause & Perimenopause
summary: The transition out of reproductive years, with hot flushes, sleep disturbance, mood change and hair thinning — supported, not medicalised.
intro: Perimenopause can begin several years before periods stop, and the fluctuation of hormones during it causes more symptoms than the eventual low levels do. Hot flushes, disturbed sleep, mood change, joint aches, vaginal dryness and hair thinning are all part of it. It is a life stage, not a disease — but the symptoms are real and treatable. Bleeding after twelve months without a period is never normal and is always investigated.
symptoms: Irregular cycles becoming further apart before stopping
Hot flushes and night sweats
Disturbed sleep and consequent fatigue
Mood swings, irritability, anxiety and low mood
Vaginal dryness and discomfort during intercourse
Joint and muscle aches
Diffuse hair thinning, particularly at the crown and parting
Reduced concentration and memory lapses
causes: Progressive decline in ovarian follicle numbers and oestrogen production
Wide hormonal fluctuation during the perimenopausal years
Surgical menopause after removal of the ovaries
Chemotherapy or radiotherapy
Premature ovarian insufficiency before 40, which needs specific assessment
Smoking, which brings menopause forward
treatment: Assessment of symptom burden, bone health risk and cardiovascular risk — this stage matters for both
Constitutional homeopathic prescription for flushes, sleep, mood and the individual pattern
Specific attention to menopausal hair thinning, which distresses many women and is often unaddressed
Guidance on calcium, vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise and sleep
Balanced discussion of hormone therapy, including referral where it is the appropriate choice

expectedResults.detail: Sleep and flush frequency are usually the first symptoms to respond.
Mood, joint aches and general resilience typically improve.
Hair thinning improves slowly and often incompletely, since the underlying hormonal shift is permanent. Bone and heart health remain long-term priorities.

faqs.question: Is hormone therapy dangerous?
faqs.answer: The picture is more nuanced than the headlines from twenty years ago suggested. For many women within ten years of menopause with significant symptoms, benefits outweigh risks. It is an individual decision worth making with proper information — this clinic will not talk you out of it on principle.

faqs.question: Will my hair grow back after menopause?
faqs.answer: Menopausal thinning usually stabilises with treatment and general health measures, but complete return to pre-menopausal density is uncommon. That is stated honestly at the outset rather than discovered after a year of treatment.

name: Uterine Fibroids
summary: Benign muscular growths in the uterine wall causing heavy bleeding, pressure and pain — managed medically, removed surgically.
intro: Fibroids are non-cancerous growths of uterine muscle, and they are very common — many women have them without ever knowing. Symptoms depend far more on position than on size: a small fibroid distorting the cavity can cause heavy bleeding, while a large one on the outer wall may cause nothing. Treatment here manages bleeding, pain and anaemia. It does not dissolve fibroids, and this clinic states that at the first consultation rather than the fifth.
symptoms: Heavy or prolonged menstrual bleeding
Pelvic pressure or a sense of fullness
Frequent urination from pressure on the bladder
Constipation from pressure on the bowel
Pain during periods or intercourse
Abdominal enlargement in larger fibroids
Anaemia, fatigue and hair fall from chronic blood loss
Difficulty conceiving or recurrent miscarriage in some positions
causes: Oestrogen and progesterone dependent growth
Genetic and familial predisposition
Earlier menarche
Obesity, which raises circulating oestrogen
Not having had children
Higher prevalence in some ethnic groups, including South Asian women
treatment: Ultrasound assessment of number, size and — most importantly — position
Haemoglobin and iron studies, since anaemia from fibroid bleeding is common
Homeopathic prescription for the bleeding pattern, pain and constitutional picture
Correction of iron deficiency and management of the associated hair fall
Gynaecology referral for rapidly growing fibroids, severe symptoms, fertility concerns or any post-menopausal growth

expectedResults.detail: Bleeding volume and pain are the practical targets and are tracked cycle by cycle.
Where bleeding settles, haemoglobin recovers and fatigue and hair fall follow.
Fibroids generally shrink only after menopause. Medicine does not dissolve them, and where they are large, growing or causing severe symptoms, surgery is the honest recommendation.

faqs.question: Can homeopathy dissolve my fibroids?
faqs.answer: No. That claim is made frequently and it is not true. What treatment can reasonably address is the bleeding, pain and anaemia they cause. If a fibroid needs removing, you will be told that plainly.

faqs.question: Do all fibroids need surgery?
faqs.answer: No — many need nothing at all beyond monitoring. Surgery is for symptoms that are not controlled, rapid growth, pressure effects, or fertility problems attributable to the fibroid's position.

name: Ovarian Cysts
summary: Fluid-filled sacs on the ovary — most are functional and resolve alone; a few need imaging follow-up or surgery.
intro: Most ovarian cysts are functional: a follicle that did not release its egg or a corpus luteum that persisted, and they resolve within two or three cycles without any treatment. Others — endometriomas, dermoids, cystadenomas — do not. Size, appearance on ultrasound and your age determine what happens next. Sudden severe one-sided pelvic pain can mean torsion or rupture and is an emergency, not something to manage at home.
symptoms: Often none — many cysts are found incidentally on a scan
Dull ache or heaviness on one side of the pelvis
Pain during intercourse
Bloating and a sense of abdominal fullness
Irregular periods
Sudden severe one-sided pain, with nausea and vomiting — an emergency
Pressure symptoms on bladder or bowel in larger cysts
causes: Normal ovulation producing functional follicular or corpus luteum cysts
Polycystic ovary syndrome
Endometriosis forming endometriomas
Developmental cysts such as dermoids
Benign tumours of ovarian tissue
Pelvic infection
Fertility medication and ovarian stimulation
treatment: Ultrasound characterisation, with tumour markers where the appearance or age warrants it
Distinguishing a functional cyst — which needs observation — from one that needs intervention
Homeopathic prescription for pain, cycle regulation and the constitutional picture
Planned repeat imaging rather than continuous treatment of something that may resolve alone
Immediate referral for large, complex or persistent cysts, and emergency referral for sudden severe pain

expectedResults.detail: Most functional cysts resolve within two to three cycles. A repeat scan documents that objectively.
Pain and cycle symptoms usually improve; persistent cysts are re-imaged rather than assumed to be settling.
Endometriomas, dermoids and complex cysts do not resolve with medicine. Surgical referral is made rather than treatment prolonged.

faqs.question: Will the cyst go away on its own?
faqs.answer: Functional cysts usually do, within two or three cycles. Endometriomas, dermoids and complex cysts do not, which is why the ultrasound characterisation matters more than the fact of a cyst being present.

faqs.question: Is an ovarian cyst dangerous?
faqs.answer: The great majority are benign. The situations that need urgency are sudden severe one-sided pain — suggesting torsion or rupture — and complex or growing cysts, particularly after menopause. Those are referred rather than treated here.

name: Endometriosis
summary: Endometrial-like tissue growing outside the uterus, causing severe period pain, pelvic pain and often difficulty conceiving.
intro: Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory condition in which tissue resembling the uterine lining grows in the pelvis, bleeding and scarring with each cycle. It takes an average of seven to ten years to be diagnosed, largely because severe period pain in young women is so routinely normalised. Treatment here manages pain and general wellbeing and works alongside gynaecological care. It does not remove endometriotic deposits, and it is not a fertility treatment.
symptoms: Severe period pain, often starting days before bleeding
Chronic pelvic pain outside periods
Deep pain during or after intercourse
Pain on passing stool or urine, particularly during periods
Heavy or irregular bleeding
Difficulty conceiving
Fatigue, bloating and bowel symptoms that flare cyclically
Pain worsening over years
causes: Retrograde menstruation depositing endometrial cells in the pelvis
Immune factors allowing that tissue to implant and persist
Genetic predisposition, with a clear familial pattern
Oestrogen-dependent growth of the deposits
Coelomic metaplasia as a proposed mechanism for distant sites
Not caused by anything the patient did or failed to do
treatment: Taking the pain history seriously and pursuing diagnosis rather than deferring it
Ultrasound, and gynaecology referral for laparoscopy where the picture warrants definitive diagnosis
Constitutional homeopathic prescription for pain, inflammation and the whole clinical picture
Attention to fatigue, bowel symptoms and the psychological weight of chronic pain
Coordination with gynaecology on hormonal or surgical management, and early referral where fertility is a concern

expectedResults.detail: Pain intensity and analgesic requirement are the practical measures used.
Many patients report fewer disabling days and better function between cycles.
Endometriosis is chronic and recurs even after surgery. Deposits and adhesions do not resolve with medicine, and treatment here does not replace gynaecological care or fertility treatment.

faqs.question: Can homeopathy cure endometriosis?
faqs.answer: No. It is a chronic condition that recurs even after surgical excision. Treatment here aims at pain, function and general wellbeing alongside gynaecological management — and it will not be described to you as anything more.

faqs.question: Will it stop me having children?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily — many women with endometriosis conceive without help. It does reduce fertility on average, and if you are trying to conceive, early referral to a fertility specialist matters more than a long course of any medicine.

name: Leucorrhoea (White Discharge)
summary: Vaginal discharge — normal in much of its variation, and needing treatment when the character, smell or associated symptoms change.
intro: Some vaginal discharge is physiological and varies naturally through the cycle. It becomes significant when it changes in colour, consistency or smell, or comes with itching, burning or pelvic pain. The common causes are candida, bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis, and they need distinguishing because their treatments differ entirely. Repeated self-treatment with over-the-counter antifungals for a discharge that is not fungal is a frequent reason it persists.
symptoms: Increased vaginal discharge beyond your usual pattern
Thick, white, curd-like discharge with intense itching, suggesting candida
Thin, grey discharge with a fishy odour, suggesting bacterial vaginosis
Frothy, greenish-yellow discharge, suggesting trichomoniasis
Burning on passing urine or during intercourse
Vulval redness, soreness and swelling
Lower abdominal pain or backache in pelvic infection
Fatigue and weakness where discharge is prolonged
causes: Candida overgrowth, often after antibiotics or in diabetes
Bacterial vaginosis from disturbed vaginal flora
Trichomoniasis, a sexually transmitted infection
Pelvic inflammatory disease
Cervical erosion or polyps
Poor glycaemic control in diabetes
Over-washing and vaginal douching, which disturb normal flora
Retained foreign body such as a forgotten tampon
treatment: Examination and, where indicated, swabs — the cause determines the treatment and cannot be assumed
Blood sugar testing where candida is recurrent, which sometimes uncovers diabetes
Homeopathic prescription for the discharge character and constitutional picture
Clear guidance on hygiene, and specifically on stopping douching and antiseptic washes
Referral for pelvic pain, fever, suspected pelvic inflammatory disease or any post-coital or post-menopausal bleeding

expectedResults.detail: Itching, burning and odour usually settle first once the correct cause is being treated.
Discharge normalises and recurrence becomes less frequent.
Recurrent candida with poorly controlled diabetes will keep returning until the diabetes is addressed. Sexually transmitted causes need the partner treated too, or reinfection is certain.

faqs.question: Is all white discharge abnormal?
faqs.answer: No. Clear or white discharge that varies through the cycle without itch, smell or pain is normal and needs no treatment. What matters is a change from your own pattern.

faqs.question: Should I use antiseptic washes?
faqs.answer: No. Antiseptic washes and douching strip the protective lactobacilli that keep the vagina healthy and are a common cause of recurrent bacterial vaginosis. Plain water externally is sufficient.

name: Difficulty Conceiving
summary: Support for the health factors that influence fertility, with clear guidance on when specialist assessment should not be delayed.
intro: Difficulty conceiving is defined as twelve months of unprotected intercourse without pregnancy — six months if you are over 35. It is not a woman's problem by default: roughly a third of causes are male, a third female and the rest shared or unexplained, which is why both partners are assessed. Age is the single most important variable and it does not wait for treatment to work. This clinic will support your general and cyclical health, and will tell you plainly when a fertility specialist is the priority.
symptoms: No pregnancy after twelve months of trying — six months if over 35
Irregular or absent periods
Very painful periods, suggesting endometriosis
Signs of PCOS: acne, excess hair growth, weight gain
History of pelvic infection or pelvic surgery
Recurrent miscarriage
Reduced libido or symptoms of thyroid disease
causes: Ovulation disorders, most commonly PCOS
Tubal damage from previous infection or surgery
Endometriosis
Thyroid dysfunction and raised prolactin
Uterine factors: fibroids, polyps, adhesions
Age-related decline in egg quality and number
Male factor — low count, motility or morphology
Weight at either extreme, smoking and alcohol
treatment: Baseline assessment of both partners, including semen analysis — this is not deferred
Thyroid, prolactin and ovulation assessment, with pelvic ultrasound
Constitutional homeopathic prescription for cycle regularity, stress and general health
Practical guidance on fertile window timing, weight, sleep and folic acid supplementation
Prompt fertility specialist referral where age, tubal disease, severe male factor or duration makes that the priority — delay costs opportunity here

expectedResults.detail: Cycle regularity, stress and general health measures are addressed; investigations are completed rather than postponed.
Where an ovulation or thyroid problem is identified and corrected, cycles typically become more predictable.
No fertility outcome is promised here — by any treatment. Where six months of general management brings no result, or where age or tubal factors apply, specialist referral is the responsible course.

faqs.question: Can homeopathy guarantee pregnancy?
faqs.answer: No, and no clinic honestly can. Treatment here supports cycle regularity, weight, thyroid health and stress — all of which influence fertility. It does not open blocked tubes, improve egg quality with age, or substitute for IVF where that is indicated.

faqs.question: Should my husband be tested too?
faqs.answer: Yes, at the start rather than after months. Male factors account for a substantial share of infertility, and a semen analysis is quick, inexpensive and frequently changes the entire direction of treatment.

name: Hirsutism (Excess Facial Hair)
summary: Coarse, dark hair in a male pattern on the face, chest or abdomen — usually hormonal, frequently PCOS, and slow to respond.
intro: Hirsutism means coarse, pigmented hair growing in areas where women typically have only fine vellus hair: upper lip, chin, chest, abdomen and back. It is distinct from generally hairy arms and legs, which is often just family or ethnic pattern. PCOS accounts for the large majority of cases. Rapid onset with voice deepening or muscle change is different — that needs urgent assessment for an androgen-secreting tumour.
symptoms: Coarse, dark hair on the upper lip, chin and jawline
Hair on the chest, around the nipples, on the abdomen or lower back
Increasing need for threading, waxing or shaving
Acne and oily skin
Irregular or absent periods
Scalp hair thinning at the crown alongside facial hair growth
Weight gain and darkened skin folds
Rapid onset with voice change or muscle bulk — needs urgent assessment
causes: Polycystic ovary syndrome, the cause in most cases
Familial and ethnic patterns of hair growth
Congenital adrenal hyperplasia in its late-onset form
Raised prolactin and thyroid dysfunction
Insulin resistance and obesity
Medications including steroids and certain hormones
Androgen-secreting ovarian or adrenal tumours — rare, but the reason rapid onset is investigated
treatment: Hormonal assessment: androgens, thyroid, prolactin, and pelvic ultrasound for PCOS
Urgent investigation where onset has been rapid or is accompanied by virilising features
Constitutional homeopathic prescription addressing the hormonal picture and cycle
Attention to insulin resistance and weight, which drive androgen levels in PCOS
Frank discussion of laser hair reduction, which is the definitive answer for hair already present

expectedResults.detail: Cycle regularity, acne and oiliness typically respond before hair growth does.
New coarse hair growth may slow. Hair follicles work on a months-long cycle, so nothing here is quick.
Hair already converted to coarse terminal hair does not revert. Removing it requires laser or electrolysis, and that is said at the outset rather than after a year of treatment.

faqs.question: Will existing facial hair disappear with treatment?
faqs.answer: No. Medical treatment can slow new growth by addressing the hormonal driver, but hair follicles already converted to coarse hair stay that way. Laser hair reduction is what removes it, and combining the two is the practical approach.

faqs.question: Does shaving make it grow thicker?
faqs.answer: No. This is a persistent myth. Shaving cuts the hair at a blunt angle so regrowth feels coarser to the touch, but it does not change the number, thickness or rate of growth of hair follicles.

name: Recurrent Urinary Infections
summary: Repeated burning, frequency and urgency — common in women, and worth treating at the pattern rather than one episode at a time.
intro: Recurrent urinary tract infection means two infections in six months or three in a year. Women are affected far more often for anatomical reasons. Each episode usually needs antibiotics, and repeated courses bring their own problems — which is why the aim here is to reduce how often episodes occur rather than to replace treatment of the episode itself. Fever with loin pain means the kidney is involved and needs urgent medical care.
symptoms: Burning or stinging on passing urine
Frequent urge to urinate, often passing very little
Urgency and lower abdominal discomfort
Cloudy, strong-smelling or blood-tinged urine
Feeling of incomplete emptying
Fever, loin pain, nausea or vomiting — kidney involvement, needing urgent care
Confusion or sudden deterioration in older women
causes: Bacteria, most often E. coli, ascending the short female urethra
Sexual activity, and delayed urination afterwards
Inadequate fluid intake and holding urine for long periods
Menopausal changes to vaginal and urethral tissue
Diabetes, particularly when poorly controlled
Incomplete bladder emptying, kidney stones or structural abnormality
Constipation
Douching and antiseptic washes disturbing protective flora
treatment: Urine culture during an episode — treating repeatedly without one is how resistance develops
Investigation for underlying causes: diabetes, stones, incomplete emptying, structural factors
Constitutional homeopathic prescription aimed at the recurrence pattern and susceptibility
Practical measures: fluid intake, voiding habits, post-coital urination, and stopping antiseptic washes
Coordination with your physician on acute antibiotic treatment, and urgent referral for fever with loin pain

expectedResults.detail: Acute symptoms are managed as they arise, usually alongside appropriate antibiotic treatment.
The measure that matters is interval between episodes — that is what treatment targets.
Where stones, incomplete emptying or poorly controlled diabetes underlie the pattern, infections continue until those are dealt with. Urology referral is made rather than the cycle repeated.

faqs.question: Can I treat a urine infection without antibiotics?
faqs.answer: An acute bacterial UTI usually needs antibiotics, and untreated infection can ascend to the kidneys. Treatment here targets how often you get them, not whether you should treat the one you have.

faqs.question: Why do I keep getting them?
faqs.answer: Usually a combination: anatomy, fluid intake, voiding habits and post-menopausal tissue changes. Sometimes there is a specific cause — a stone, incomplete emptying or diabetes — which is exactly why the workup happens rather than another course of tablets.

name: Recurrent Cold & Cough
summary: Children who seem to catch one infection after another — usually normal immune development, sometimes something worth investigating.
intro: Six to eight viral infections a year is normal for a preschool child, and more still in the first year of daycare or school. That is the immune system learning, not failing. What is worth attention is infection that is unusually severe, slow to clear, or accompanied by poor weight gain. Treatment here supports resilience between episodes and — just as importantly — reduces the antibiotic courses that most of these children do not need.
symptoms: Frequent episodes of runny nose, cough and mild fever
Cough lingering two to three weeks after each cold
Blocked nose disturbing sleep and feeding
Reduced appetite during and after episodes
Irritability and tiredness
Episodes clustering after starting school or daycare
Wheeze during episodes in some children — worth specific assessment
causes: Normal immune development with high exposure at school and daycare
Underlying allergic rhinitis presenting as recurrent 'colds'
Enlarged adenoids obstructing drainage
Passive smoke exposure and indoor air pollution
Damp housing and mould
Iron deficiency and inadequate nutrition
Vitamin D deficiency
Rarely, an immune deficiency — suspected when infections are severe or unusual
treatment: Distinguishing normal frequency from a pattern that warrants investigation
Assessment for allergic rhinitis, adenoid enlargement and asthma, which explain many 'recurrent colds'
Constitutional homeopathic prescription for susceptibility, appetite and recovery
Checking haemoglobin, iron and vitamin D where the picture suggests deficiency
Paediatric referral for poor weight gain, unusually severe infection or suspected immune deficiency

expectedResults.detail: Episode severity and recovery time are usually what change first.
Intervals between episodes typically lengthen; appetite and energy between them improve.
Frequency naturally falls as children get older and exposure builds immunity. Some improvement credited to treatment is simply the child growing up, and that is worth saying honestly.

faqs.question: Is my child's immunity weak?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Six to eight colds a year in a preschool child is normal, and more in the first year at school. Genuine immune deficiency shows itself through severe, unusual or slow-to-clear infections and poor growth — not through frequent ordinary colds.

faqs.question: Do these need antibiotics?
faqs.answer: Almost never. These are viral, and antibiotics do nothing against viruses while causing gut disturbance and resistance. Reducing unnecessary courses is one of the practical benefits of treating the pattern rather than each episode.

name: Tonsillitis
summary: Repeated painful throat infections with fever — treated to reduce recurrence, with clear criteria for when surgery is genuinely warranted.
intro: Tonsillitis is inflammation of the tonsils, usually viral and occasionally streptococcal. Recurrent attacks disrupt school, sleep and eating, and many families are offered tonsillectomy early. There are established criteria for when surgery is justified — roughly seven episodes in a year, five a year for two years, or three a year for three years — and treatment here aims to keep children below that threshold where possible, not to talk them out of surgery that is warranted.
symptoms: Sore throat with pain on swallowing
Fever, often high, with chills
Enlarged, red tonsils, sometimes with white spots
Tender, swollen glands in the neck
Bad breath
Refusal to eat or drink from throat pain
Headache, tummy pain and general unwellness
Voice change and snoring during episodes
causes: Viral infection, the cause in most episodes
Group A streptococcus, which needs specific treatment
Close contact at school and among siblings
Enlarged tonsils and adenoids retaining infection
Allergic rhinitis and post-nasal drip
Passive smoke exposure
Poor nutrition and low iron
treatment: Assessment of each episode's character, and throat swab where streptococcal infection is likely
Constitutional homeopathic prescription directed at recurrence rather than the acute episode alone
Nutritional review with attention to iron and vitamin D
Assessment for associated allergic rhinitis and adenoid enlargement
ENT referral where frequency meets surgical criteria, or where there is sleep apnoea, difficulty swallowing or an abscess

expectedResults.detail: Episode severity, fever duration and school days lost are the practical measures.
Many children have fewer and milder episodes over a treatment year.
Where episodes continue at surgical frequency, or where breathing is obstructed during sleep, tonsillectomy is the right answer and will be recommended rather than delayed.

faqs.question: Can we avoid tonsillectomy?
faqs.answer: Often, where episodes are moderate in frequency. But if your child meets the established criteria, or has obstructive sleep apnoea, surgery is the appropriate treatment and delaying it for a year of medicine is not in the child's interest.

faqs.question: Do tonsils serve a purpose?
faqs.answer: They are part of the immune system, more active in early childhood. Removing them when genuinely indicated does not leave a child immunodeficient — the rest of the immune system compensates without difficulty.

name: Adenoid Enlargement
summary: Blocked nose, mouth breathing and snoring from enlarged adenoids — with sleep-disordered breathing the reason it must not be ignored.
intro: Adenoids sit behind the nose and are naturally larger in young children, shrinking through later childhood. When enlarged enough to obstruct, they cause mouth breathing, snoring, recurrent ear and sinus problems, and in some children pauses in breathing during sleep. That last one matters most: obstructive sleep apnoea in children affects growth, behaviour and school performance, and it is the clearest indication for surgery.
symptoms: Persistent nasal blockage and mouth breathing, including while awake
Snoring, and in some children pauses in breathing during sleep
Restless sleep, unusual sleeping positions, daytime tiredness
Nasal-sounding speech
Recurrent ear infections or hearing difficulty
Recurrent sinus infections
Poor appetite and slow weight gain
Irritability, poor concentration and behavioural change from disturbed sleep
causes: Normal lymphoid enlargement of early childhood
Repeated upper respiratory infections
Allergic rhinitis
Passive smoke exposure and indoor pollution
Chronic sinus infection
Reflux in some children
Family predisposition
treatment: Assessment of the degree of obstruction, and specific questioning about sleep and breathing pauses
Treating associated allergic rhinitis, which often accounts for much of the blockage
Constitutional homeopathic prescription for the lymphoid tendency and recurrent infection
Practical measures: saline irrigation, allergen reduction, removing smoke exposure
ENT referral where there is sleep apnoea, hearing loss, failure to thrive or persistent severe obstruction

expectedResults.detail: Nasal blockage and snoring frequency are the practical day-to-day measures.
Where allergy is a significant contributor, breathing and sleep often improve considerably.
Adenoids usually shrink naturally by around age seven to ten. Where sleep apnoea is present, waiting for that is not appropriate — adenoidectomy is, and will be recommended.

faqs.question: Will the adenoids shrink on their own?
faqs.answer: In most children, yes, over several years. The question is whether the obstruction can be safely waited out — and where there is sleep apnoea, hearing loss or poor growth, it cannot.

faqs.question: Why does snoring matter in a child?
faqs.answer: Because obstructed sleep affects growth hormone release, daytime behaviour, attention and school performance. A child who snores loudly every night, gasps or stops breathing needs assessment rather than reassurance.

name: Childhood Asthma
summary: Recurrent wheeze, cough and breathlessness in children — treated alongside inhalers, which are never stopped on our advice.
intro: Asthma in children shows itself as recurrent wheeze, night cough and breathlessness, often triggered by infection, exercise or allergens. Many families are anxious about inhalers and delay them, which is the single most common reason childhood asthma stays poorly controlled. Treatment here addresses the allergic tendency and general resilience alongside inhaler therapy. It is never a reason to stop a preventer inhaler.
symptoms: Recurrent wheezing, especially with colds
Night cough that wakes the child
Breathlessness or difficulty keeping up when playing
Chest tightness the child may describe as tummy ache
Symptoms triggered by dust, smoke, cold air, exercise or laughing
Prolonged cough after every viral infection
Reduced activity that the family has quietly normalised
causes: Inherited allergic tendency, usually with eczema or allergic rhinitis in the family
House dust mite, the leading indoor allergen locally
Viral respiratory infections
Passive smoke exposure, mosquito coils and incense
Damp housing and mould
Cold air, humidity change and the monsoon
Exercise and, occasionally, emotional excitement
treatment: Assessment of control: night cough, activity limitation and reliever use
Constitutional homeopathic prescription for the allergic tendency and episode frequency
Systematic trigger identification and practical household allergen reduction
Checking inhaler and spacer technique — very often the actual problem
A written action plan for attacks, with clear thresholds for emergency care

expectedResults.detail: Night cough and reliever inhaler use are the measures used, not how the child seems on a good day.
Many children have fewer episodes and better exercise tolerance over a treatment year.
Many children improve substantially through adolescence. Any reduction in preventer inhaler dose is your paediatrician's decision, made on sustained control.

faqs.question: Will my child be on inhalers forever?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily — many children need much less as they grow. But that decision comes from sustained good control assessed by your paediatrician, not from stopping when the child seems well for a fortnight.

faqs.question: Are inhalers harmful for children?
faqs.answer: No. Inhaled steroid doses are small and delivered directly to the airways. The harm in childhood asthma comes overwhelmingly from undertreatment — repeated attacks, missed school and emergency visits — not from the inhaler.

name: Recurrent Ear Infections
summary: Repeated middle ear infection and fluid — painful, common, and important because persistent fluid affects hearing and speech.
intro: Middle ear infection is very common in young children because the Eustachian tube is short and horizontal. Most episodes settle, and most do not need antibiotics. What needs watching is fluid that persists after the infection clears: it muffles hearing, and in a child learning to speak, months of muffled hearing has consequences for language development. That is the reason ear infections in children are followed up rather than simply treated.
symptoms: Ear pain, often worse lying down at night
Fever and irritability
Tugging or rubbing at the ear in younger children
Discharge from the ear if the eardrum perforates
Reduced hearing, or turning up the television volume
Not responding when called, or appearing inattentive
Delayed or unclear speech in longstanding fluid
Balance problems and clumsiness
causes: Short, horizontal Eustachian tube in young children
Upper respiratory infections
Enlarged adenoids obstructing tube drainage
Allergic rhinitis
Bottle feeding while lying flat
Passive smoke exposure
Daycare attendance and sibling exposure
Cleft palate and certain syndromes
treatment: Examination of the eardrum, and hearing assessment where fluid has persisted
Treating the underlying contributors — adenoids, allergic rhinitis — rather than each episode in isolation
Constitutional homeopathic prescription for the recurrence pattern and general susceptibility
Practical measures: upright feeding, smoke removal, allergen reduction
ENT referral for persistent fluid beyond three months, hearing loss, speech delay or frequent recurrence

expectedResults.detail: Pain and acute episodes are managed as they arise, with antibiotics where genuinely indicated.
Frequency of episodes is the target; fluid clearance is checked rather than assumed.
Persistent fluid with hearing loss affects speech development and is not waited out indefinitely. Grommets are sometimes the right answer, and will be recommended when they are.

faqs.question: Does every ear infection need antibiotics?
faqs.answer: No. Most resolve without them, and guidelines in many countries now advise watchful waiting with pain relief in older children who are not severely unwell. Very young children and severe cases are treated differently.

faqs.question: Could this be affecting my child's speech?
